entries.notes:

entries.name: epoch
entries.notes:
The epoch of the version.

>>> Version("2.0.0").epoch
0
>>> Version("1!2.0.0").epoch
1

entries.name: release
entries.notes:
The components of the "release" segment of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").release
(1, 2, 3)
>>> Version("2.0.0").release
(2, 0, 0)
>>> Version("1!2.0.0.post0").release
(2, 0, 0)

Includes trailing zeroes but not the epoch or any pre-release / development /
post-release suffixes.

entries.name: pre
entries.notes:
The pre-release segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").pre)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3a1").pre
('a', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3b1").pre
('b', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3rc1").pre
('rc', 1)

entries.name: post
entries.notes:
The post-release number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").post)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.post1").post
1

entries.name: dev
entries.notes:
The development number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").dev)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.dev1").dev
1

entries.name: local
entries.notes:
The local version segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").local)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").local
'abc'

entries.name: public
entries.notes:
The public portion of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").public
'1!1.2.3.dev1'

entries.name: base_version
entries.notes:
The "base version" of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").base_version
'1!1.2.3'

The "base version" is the public version of the project without any pre or post
release markers.

>>> Version("1.2.3").is_prerelease
False
>>> Version("1.2.3a1").is_prerelease

>>> Version("1.2.3b1").is_prerelease
True
>>> Version("1.2.3rc1").is_prerelease
True
>>> Version("1.2.3dev1").is_prerelease

>>> Version("1.2.3.dev1").is_devrelease
True

1

entries.notes:

>>> Version("1.2.3").minor
2
>>> Version("1").minor
0

3

entries.name: ansiformat
entries.notes:
Format ``text`` with a color and/or some attributes::

    color       normal color
    *color*     bold color
    _color_     underlined color
    +color+     blinking color

entries.name: apply_filters
entries.notes:
Use this method to apply an iterable of filters to
a stream. If lexer is given it's forwarded to the
filter, otherwise the filter receives `None`.

entries.name: simplefilter
Filter
entries.notes:
Default filter. Subclass this class or use the `simplefilter`
decorator to create own filters.

entries.name: FunctionFilter
entries.notes:
Abstract class used by `simplefilter` to create simple
function filters on the fly. The `simplefilter` decorator
automatically creates subclasses of this class for
functions passed to it.

entries.name: Formatter
entries.notes:
Converts a token stream to text.

Formatters should have attributes to help selecting them. These
are similar to the corresponding :class:`~pygments.lexer.Lexer`
attributes.

.. autoattribute:: name
   :no-value:

.. autoattribute:: aliases
   :no-value:

.. autoattribute:: filenames
   :no-value:

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
As with lexers, this constructor takes arbitrary optional arguments,
and if you override it, you should first process your own options, then
call the base class implementation.

entries.name: get_style_defs
entries.notes:
This method must return statements or declarations suitable to define
the current style for subsequent highlighted text (e.g. CSS classes
in the `HTMLFormatter`).

The optional argument `arg` can be used to modify the generation and
is formatter dependent (it is standardized because it can be given

entries.name: format
entries.notes:
This method must format the tokens from the `tokensource` iterable and
write the formatted version to the file object `outfile`.

Formatter options can control how exactly the tokens are converted.

entries.name: LexerMeta
entries.notes:
This metaclass automagically converts ``analyse_text`` methods into
static methods which always return float values.

entries.name: Lexer
entries.notes:
Lexer for a specific language.

See also :doc:`lexerdevelopment`, a high-level guide to writing
lexers.

Lexer classes have attributes used for choosing the most appropriate
lexer based on various criteria.

.. autoattribute:: name
   :no-value:
.. autoattribute:: aliases
   :no-value:
.. autoattrib

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
This constructor takes arbitrary options as keyword arguments.
Every subclass must first process its own options and then call
the `Lexer` constructor, since it processes the basic
options like `stripnl`.

An example looks like this:

.. sourcecode:: python

   def __init__(self, **options):

entries.name: add_filter
entries.notes: Add a new stream filter to this lexer.

entries.name: analyse_text
entries.notes:
A static method which is called for lexer guessing.

It should analyse the text and return a float in the range
from ``0.0`` to ``1.0``.  If it returns ``0.0``, the lexer
will not be selected as the most probable one, if it returns
``1.0``, it will be selected immediately.  This is used by
`guess_le

entries.name: _preprocess_lexer_input
entries.notes: Apply preprocessing such as decoding the input, removing BOM and normalizing newlines.

entries.name: get_tokens
entries.notes:
This method is the basic interface of a lexer. It is called by
the `highlight()` function. It must process the text and return an
iterable of ``(tokentype, value)`` pairs from `text`.

Normally, you don't need to override this method. The default
implementation processes the options recognized by al

entries.name: get_tokens_unprocessed
entries.notes:
This method should process the text and return an iterable of
``(index, tokentype, value)`` tuples where ``index`` is the starting
position of the token within the input text.

It must be overridden by subclasses. It is recommended to
implement it as a generator to maximize effectiveness.

entries.name: DelegatingLexer
entries.notes:
This lexer takes two lexer as arguments. A root lexer and
a language lexer. First everything is scanned using the language
lexer, afterwards all ``Other`` tokens are lexed using the root
lexer.

The lexers from the ``template`` lexer package use this base lexer.

entries.name: include
entries.notes: Indicates that a state should include rules from another state.

entries.name: _inherit
entries.notes: Indicates the a state should inherit from its superclass.

entries.name: combined
entries.notes: Indicates a state combined from multiple states.

entries.name: _PseudoMatch
entries.notes: A pseudo match object constructed from a string.

entries.name: bygroups
entries.notes: Callback that yields multiple actions for each group in the match.

entries.name: _This
entries.notes:
Special singleton used for indicating the caller class.
Used by ``using``.

entries.name: using
entries.notes:
Callback that processes the match with a different lexer.

The keyword arguments are forwarded to the lexer, except `state` which
is handled separately.

`state` specifies the state that the new lexer will start in, and can
be an enumerable such as ('root', 'inline', 'string') or a simple
string whi

entries.name: default
entries.notes:
Indicates a state or state action (e.g. #pop) to apply.
For example default('#pop') is equivalent to ('', Token, '#pop')
Note that state tuples may be used as well.

.. versionadded:: 2.0

entries.name: words
entries.notes:
Indicates a list of literal words that is transformed into an optimized
regex that matches any of the words.

.. versionadded:: 2.0

entries.notes:
Metaclass for RegexLexer, creates the self._tokens attribute from
self.tokens on the first instantiation.

entries.notes: Preprocess the regular expression component of a token definition.

entries.name: _process_token
entries.notes: Preprocess the token component of a token definition.

entries.name: _process_new_state
entries.notes: Preprocess the state transition action of a token definition.

entries.name: _process_state
entries.notes: Preprocess a single state definition.

entries.name: process_tokendef
entries.notes: Preprocess a dictionary of token definitions.

entries.name: get_tokendefs
entries.notes:
Merge tokens from superclasses in MRO order, returning a single tokendef
dictionary.

Any state that is not defined by a subclass will be inherited
automatically.  States that *are* defined by subclasses will, by
default, override that state in the superclass.  If a subclass wishes to
inherit defini

entries.name: __call__
entries.notes: Instantiate cls after preprocessing its token definitions.

entries.name: RegexLexer
entries.notes:
Base for simple stateful regular expression-based lexers.
Simplifies the lexing process so that you need only
provide a list of states and regular expressions.

entries.name: LexerContext
entries.notes: A helper object that holds lexer position data.

entries.name: ExtendedRegexLexer
entries.notes: A RegexLexer that uses a context object to store its state.

entries.name: do_insertions
entries.notes:
Helper for lexers which must combine the results of several
sublexers.

``insertions`` is a list of ``(index, itokens)`` pairs.
Each ``itokens`` iterable should be inserted at position
``index`` into the token stream given by the ``tokens``
argument.

The result is a combined token stream.

TODO: cl

entries.notes: Metaclass for ProfilingRegexLexer, collects regex timing info.

entries.name: ProfilingRegexLexer
entries.notes: Drop-in replacement for RegexLexer that does profiling of its regexes.

entries.name: get_filetype_from_buffer
entries.notes: Scan the buffer for modelines and return filetype if one is found.

entries.name: regex_opt_inner
entries.notes: Return a regex that matches any string in the sorted list of strings.

entries.name: regex_opt
entries.notes:
Return a compiled regex that matches any string in the given list.

The strings to match must be literal strings, not regexes.  They will be
regex-escaped.

*prefix* and *suffix* are pre- and appended to the final regex.

entries.name: EndOfText
entries.notes:
Raise if end of text is reached and the user
tried to call a match function.

entries.name: Scanner
entries.notes:
Simple scanner

All method patterns are regular expression strings (not
compiled expressions!)

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
:param text:    The text which should be scanned
:param flags:   default regular expression flags

entries.name: eos
entries.notes: `True` if the scanner reached the end of text.

entries.name: check
entries.notes:
Apply `pattern` on the current position and return
the match object. (Doesn't touch pos). Use this for
lookahead.

entries.name: test
entries.notes:
Apply a pattern on the current position and check
if it patches. Doesn't touch pos.

entries.name: scan
entries.notes:
Scan the text for the given pattern and update pos/match
and related fields. The return value is a boolean that
indicates if the pattern matched. The matched value is
stored on the instance as ``match``, the last value is
stored as ``last``. ``start_pos`` is the position of the
pointer before the pa

entries.name: get_char
entries.notes: Scan exactly one char.

entries.name: PygmentsDoc
entries.notes:
A directive to collect all lexers/formatters/filters and generate
autoclass directives for them.

entries.name: document_lexers_overview
entries.notes:
Generate a tabular overview of all lexers.

The columns are the lexer name, the extensions handled by this lexer
(or "None"), the aliases and a link to the lexer class.

entries.name: write_row
entries.notes: Format a table row

entries.name: write_seperator
entries.notes: Write a table separator row

entries.name: is_token_subtype
entries.notes:
Return True if ``ttype`` is a subtype of ``other``.

exists for backwards compatibility. use ``ttype in other`` now.

entries.name: string_to_tokentype
entries.notes:
Convert a string into a token type::

    >>> string_to_token('String.Double')
    Token.Literal.String.Double
    >>> string_to_token('Token.Literal.Number')
    Token.Literal.Number
    >>> string_to_token('')
    Token

Tokens that are already tokens are returned unchanged:

    >>> string_to_tok

entries.name: ClassNotFound
entries.notes: Raised if one of the lookup functions didn't find a matching class.

entries.name: OptionError
entries.notes:
This exception will be raised by all option processing functions if
the type or value of the argument is not correct.

entries.name: get_choice_opt
entries.notes:
If the key `optname` from the dictionary is not in the sequence
`allowed`, raise an error, otherwise return it.

entries.name: get_bool_opt
entries.notes:
Intuitively, this is `options.get(optname, default)`, but restricted to
Boolean value. The Booleans can be represented as string, in order to accept
Boolean value from the command line arguments. If the key `optname` is
present in the dictionary `options` and is not associated with a Boolean,
raise

entries.name: get_int_opt
entries.notes: As :func:`get_bool_opt`, but interpret the value as an integer.

entries.name: get_list_opt
entries.notes:
If the key `optname` from the dictionary `options` is a string,
split it at whitespace and return it. If it is already a list
or a tuple, it is returned as a list.

entries.name: make_analysator
entries.notes: Return a static text analyser function that returns float values.

entries.name: shebang_matches
entries.notes:
Check if the given regular expression matches the last part of the
shebang if one exists.

    >>> from pygments.util import shebang_matches
    >>> shebang_matches('#!/usr/bin/env python', r'python(2\.\d)?')
    True
    >>> shebang_matches('#!/usr/bin/python2.4', r'python(2\.\d)?')
    True
    >>

entries.name: doctype_matches
entries.notes:
Check if the doctype matches a regular expression (if present).

Note that this method only checks the first part of a DOCTYPE.
eg: 'html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN"'

entries.name: html_doctype_matches
entries.notes: Check if the file looks like it has a html doctype.

entries.name: looks_like_xml
entries.notes: Check if a doctype exists or if we have some tags.

entries.name: surrogatepair
entries.notes:
Given a unicode character code with length greater than 16 bits,
return the two 16 bit surrogate pair.

entries.name: format_lines
entries.notes: Formats a sequence of strings for output.

entries.name: duplicates_removed
entries.notes:
Returns a list with duplicates removed from the iterable `it`.

Order is preserved.

entries.name: Future
entries.notes:
Generic class to defer some work.

Handled specially in RegexLexerMeta, to support regex string construction at
first use.

entries.name: guess_decode
entries.notes:
Decode *text* with guessed encoding.

First try UTF-8; this should fail for non-UTF-8 encodings.
Then try the preferred locale encoding.
Fall back to latin-1, which always works.

entries.name: guess_decode_from_terminal
entries.notes:
Decode *text* coming from terminal *term*.

First try the terminal encoding, if given.
Then try UTF-8.  Then try the preferred locale encoding.
Fall back to latin-1, which always works.

entries.name: terminal_encoding
entries.notes: Return our best guess of encoding for the given *term*.

entries.name: lex
entries.notes:
Lex `code` with the `lexer` (must be a `Lexer` instance)
and return an iterable of tokens. Currently, this only calls
`lexer.get_tokens()`.

entries.name: format
entries.notes:
Format ``tokens`` (an iterable of tokens) with the formatter ``formatter``
(a `Formatter` instance).

If ``outfile`` is given and a valid file object (an object with a
``write`` method), the result will be written to it, otherwise it
is returned as a string.

entries.name: highlight
entries.notes:
This is the most high-level highlighting function. It combines `lex` and
`format` in one function.

entries.name: find_filter_class
entries.notes: Lookup a filter by name. Return None if not found.

entries.name: get_filter_by_name
entries.notes:
Return an instantiated filter.

Options are passed to the filter initializer if wanted.
Raise a ClassNotFound if not found.

entries.name: get_all_filters
entries.notes: Return a generator of all filter names.

entries.name: CodeTagFilter
entries.notes:
Highlight special code tags in comments and docstrings.

Options accepted:

`codetags` : list of strings
   A list of strings that are flagged as code tags.  The default is to
   highlight ``XXX``, ``TODO``, ``FIXME``, ``BUG`` and ``NOTE``.

.. versionchanged:: 2.13
   Now recognizes ``FIXME`` by de

entries.name: SymbolFilter
entries.notes:
Convert mathematical symbols such as \<longrightarrow> in Isabelle
or \longrightarrow in LaTeX into Unicode characters.

entries.name: Version
entries.notes:
This class abstracts handling of a project's versions.

A :class:`Version` instance is comparison aware and can be compared and
sorted using the standard Python interfaces.

>>> v1 = Version("1.0a5")
>>> v2 = Version("1.0")
>>> v1
<Version('1.0a5')>
>>> v2
<Version('1.0')>
>>> v1 < v2
True
>>> v1 ==

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
Initialize a Version object.

:param version:
    The string representation of a version which will be parsed and normalized
    before use.
:raises InvalidVersion:
    If the ``version`` does not conform to PEP 440 in any way then this
    exception will be raised.

entries.name: __repr__
entries.notes:
A representation of the Version that shows all internal state.

>>> Version('1.0.0')
<Version('1.0.0')>

entries.name: __str__
entries.notes:
A string representation of the version that can be round-tripped.

>>> str(Version("1.0a5"))
'1.0a5'

entries.name: epoch
entries.notes:
The epoch of the version.

>>> Version("2.0.0").epoch
0
>>> Version("1!2.0.0").epoch
1

entries.name: release
entries.notes:
The components of the "release" segment of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").release
(1, 2, 3)
>>> Version("2.0.0").release
(2, 0, 0)
>>> Version("1!2.0.0.post0").release
(2, 0, 0)

Includes trailing zeroes but not the epoch or any pre-release / development /
post-release suffixes.

entries.name: pre
entries.notes:
The pre-release segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").pre)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3a1").pre
('a', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3b1").pre
('b', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3rc1").pre
('rc', 1)

entries.name: post
entries.notes:
The post-release number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").post)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.post1").post
1

entries.name: dev
entries.notes:
The development number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").dev)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.dev1").dev
1

entries.name: local
entries.notes:
The local version segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").local)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").local
'abc'

entries.name: public
entries.notes:
The public portion of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").public
'1!1.2.3.dev1'

entries.name: base_version
entries.notes:
The "base version" of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").base_version
'1!1.2.3'

The "base version" is the public version of the project without any pre or post
release markers.

entries.notes:

entries.name: epoch
entries.notes:
The epoch of the version.

>>> Version("2.0.0").epoch
0
>>> Version("1!2.0.0").epoch
1

entries.name: release
entries.notes:
The components of the "release" segment of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").release
(1, 2, 3)
>>> Version("2.0.0").release
(2, 0, 0)
>>> Version("1!2.0.0.post0").release
(2, 0, 0)

Includes trailing zeroes but not the epoch or any pre-release / development /
post-release suffixes.

entries.name: pre
entries.notes:
The pre-release segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").pre)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3a1").pre
('a', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3b1").pre
('b', 1)
>>> Version("1.2.3rc1").pre
('rc', 1)

entries.name: post
entries.notes:
The post-release number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").post)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.post1").post
1

entries.name: dev
entries.notes:
The development number of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").dev)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3.dev1").dev
1

entries.name: local
entries.notes:
The local version segment of the version.

>>> print(Version("1.2.3").local)
None
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").local
'abc'

entries.name: public
entries.notes:
The public portion of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").public
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").public
'1!1.2.3.dev1'

entries.name: base_version
entries.notes:
The "base version" of the version.

>>> Version("1.2.3").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1.2.3+abc").base_version
'1.2.3'
>>> Version("1!1.2.3dev1+abc").base_version
'1!1.2.3'

The "base version" is the public version of the project without any pre or post
release markers.

>>> Version("1.2.3").is_prerelease
False
>>> Version("1.2.3a1").is_prerelease

>>> Version("1.2.3b1").is_prerelease
True
>>> Version("1.2.3rc1").is_prerelease
True
>>> Version("1.2.3dev1").is_prerelease

>>> Version("1.2.3.dev1").is_devrelease
True

1

entries.notes:

>>> Version("1.2.3").minor
2
>>> Version("1").minor
0

3

    *color*     bold color

    +color+     blinking color

entries.name: apply_filters
entries.notes:
Use this method to apply an iterable of filters to
a stream. If lexer is given it's forwarded to the
filter, otherwise the filter receives `None`.

entries.name: simplefilter
Filter
entries.notes:
Default filter. Subclass this class or use the `simplefilter`
decorator to create own filters.

entries.name: FunctionFilter
entries.notes:
Abstract class used by `simplefilter` to create simple
function filters on the fly. The `simplefilter` decorator
automatically creates subclasses of this class for
functions passed to it.

entries.name: Formatter
entries.notes:
Converts a token stream to text.

Formatters should have attributes to help selecting them. These
are similar to the corresponding :class:`~pygments.lexer.Lexer`
attributes.

.. autoattribute:: name
   :no-value:

.. autoattribute:: aliases
   :no-value:

.. autoattribute:: filenames
   :no-value:

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
As with lexers, this constructor takes arbitrary optional arguments,
and if you override it, you should first process your own options, then
call the base class implementation.

entries.name: get_style_defs
entries.notes:
This method must return statements or declarations suitable to define
the current style for subsequent highlighted text (e.g. CSS classes
in the `HTMLFormatter`).

The optional argument `arg` can be used to modify the generation and
is formatter dependent (it is standardized because it can be given

entries.name: format
entries.notes:
This method must format the tokens from the `tokensource` iterable and
write the formatted version to the file object `outfile`.

Formatter options can control how exactly the tokens are converted.

entries.name: LexerMeta
entries.notes:
This metaclass automagically converts ``analyse_text`` methods into
static methods which always return float values.

entries.name: Lexer
entries.notes:
Lexer for a specific language.

See also :doc:`lexerdevelopment`, a high-level guide to writing
lexers.

Lexer classes have attributes used for choosing the most appropriate
lexer based on various criteria.

.. autoattribute:: name
   :no-value:
.. autoattribute:: aliases
   :no-value:
.. autoattrib

entries.name: __init__
entries.notes:
This constructor takes arbitrary options as keyword arguments.
Every subclass must first process its own options and then call
the `Lexer` constructor, since it processes the basic
options like `stripnl`.

An example looks like this:

.. sourcecode:: python

   def __init__(self, **options):

entries.name: add_filter
entries.notes: Add a new stream filter to this lexer.

entries.name: analyse_text
entries.notes:
A static method which is called for lexer guessing.

It should analyse the text and return a float in the range
from ``0.0`` to ``1.0``.  If it returns ``0.0``, the lexer
will not be selected as the most probable one, if it returns
``1.0``, it will be selected immediately.  This is used by
`guess_le

entries.name: _preprocess_lexer_input
entries.notes: Apply preprocessing such as decoding the input, removing BOM and normalizing newlines.

entries.name: get_tokens
entries.notes:
This method is the basic interface of a lexer. It is called by
the `highlight()` function. It must process the text and return an
iterable of ``(tokentype, value)`` pairs from `text`.

Normally, you don't need to override this method. The default
implementation processes the options recognized by al

entries.name: get_tokens_unprocessed
entries.notes:
This method should process the text and return an iterable of
``(index, tokentype, value)`` tuples where ``index`` is the starting
position of the token within the input text.

It must be overridden by subclasses. It is recommended to
implement it as a generator to maximize effectiveness.

entries.name: DelegatingLexer
entries.notes:
This lexer takes two lexer as arguments. A root lexer and
a language lexer. First everything is scanned using the language
lexer, afterwards all ``Other`` tokens are lexed using the root
lexer.

The lexers from the ``template`` lexer package use this base lexer.

The keyword arguments are forwarded to the lexer, except `state` which
is handled separately.

be an enumerable such as ('root', 'inline', 'string') or a simple
string whi

entries.name: default
entries.notes:
Indicates a state or state action (e.g. #pop) to apply.
For example default('#pop') is equivalent to ('', Token, '#pop')
Note that state tuples may be used as well.

Indicates a list of literal words that is transformed into an optimized
regex that matches any of the words.

entries.name: __call__
entries.notes: Instantiate cls after preprocessing its token definitions.

entries.name: RegexLexer
entries.notes:
Base for simple stateful regular expression-based lexers.
Simplifies the lexing process so that you need only
provide a list of states and regular expressions.

entries.name: LexerContext
entries.notes: A helper object that holds lexer position data.

entries.name: ExtendedRegexLexer
entries.notes: A RegexLexer that uses a context object to store its state.

entries.name: do_insertions
entries.notes:
Helper for lexers which must combine the results of several
sublexers.

``insertions`` is a list of ``(index, itokens)`` pairs.
Each ``itokens`` iterable should be inserted at position
``index`` into the token stream given by the ``tokens``
argument.

The result is a combined token stream.
